I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` workflow to ground the refactor in the actual function signatures and call sites, then I’ll give a scoped file-change/API proposal without modifying code.

The local shell does not have a global `crimes` binary, so I’m treating the supplied JSON as the authoritative scan result. I’ve confirmed the fixture files exist and am now checking their exact exports and behavioral differences so the proposed helper preserves today’s API.

The scan confirms one medium-severity `near_duplicate_block`: the same sanitisation algorithm appears in three files, differing only in function and local-variable names.

Proposed refactor:

```ts
// src/sanitize.ts
export function sanitizeText(
  value: string | null | undefined,
): string;
```

`sanitizeText` should own the complete pipeline: null handling, trimming, control-character removal, whitespace normalization, 1,000-character limit, unsafe-prefix/escape rejection, punctuation filtering, and uppercase normalization.

To avoid breaking current consumers, keep the existing exports as thin wrappers:

```ts
export function sanitizeUserInput(raw: string): string {
  return sanitizeText(raw);
}
```

Do the equivalent for `sanitizeText` in `sanitize-b.ts`—importing the shared helper under an alias—and `cleanMessage` in `sanitize-c.ts`.

Files affected:

- Add `src/sanitize.ts` containing the consolidated implementation.
- Modify [sanitize-a.ts](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-a.ts:10) to delegate `sanitizeUserInput`.
- Modify [sanitize-b.ts](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-b.ts:9) to delegate `sanitizeText`.
- Modify [sanitize-c.ts](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-c.ts:9) to delegate `cleanMessage`.
- Add a focused `sanitize.test.ts` if tests are introduced, covering every rejection and normalization branch.

The `assertAdminA/B/C` exports should remain untouched in this refactor. They represent a separate policy finding and are not behaviorally equivalent—particularly `assertAdminC`, which returns true for non-admins. Likewise, the telemetry duplication is a separate refactor.
